But opponents say the violence that marked the final months of his mandate should disqualify him from the role.

rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has said there would be "zero tolerance" for arson after France was hit by wildfires that have scorched thousands of hectares, as multiple heatwaves since May have dried out forests and fields. Dozens have been arrested across the country over starting fires, including a volunteer firefighter.

rfi.title: Fears over foreign influence in France, as Musk backs Le Pen presidential bid

rfi.title: French man charged with rape and murder of schoolgirl Lyhanna
rfi.description: The main suspect in the death of an 11-year-old girl whose body was found in the Gers region has been charged with the rape and murder of a child. The case has sparked nationwide protests and renewed scrutiny of the French justice system, after it emerged that the suspect had previously been accused of raping another child.

rfi.title: Greenpeace Africa demands halt to $17bn Kenya coastal oil refinery

rfi.title: French parliament passes assisted dying law after years of wrangling

rfi.title: Students in Cameroon protest new financial requirements for French visas
rfi.description: Dozens of people took to the streets outside the French embassy in Yaoundé this week to protest new rules that require Cameroonian nationals to demonstrate the means to pay tuition fees in full before they can obtain a student visa for France. Protesters say the policy will make studying in France impossible for many people who already have places at French institutions for the coming academic year.

rfi.title: EU and Ukraine seal drone deal to pair industry with battlefield expertise
rfi.description: European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday announced a drone deal with Ukraine to boost joint production of the key battlefield technology.

rfi.title: Lawyers vow to fight on after Kenya court rejects Rastafarians' cannabis bid
rfi.description: In a long-awaited ruling, Kenya's High Court has rejected a bid by Rastafarians to be allowed to smoke cannabis as part of their religious worship. But lawyers say the fight continues and the case has opened up debate on the country's drug laws and what constitutes religious freedom.

rfi.title: Firefighters tackle flare-ups in Fontainebleau forest after reining in blaze
rfi.description: Around 800 firefighters were still at work in Fontainebleau forest on Wednesday morning, tackling flare-ups after the fires were brought under control the previous day, following 48 hours of intense firefighting.

President Emmanuel Macron is due to lead the main memorial ceremony later on Tuesday, while a minute's silence will be observed before France's World Cup semi-final against Spain.

lemonde.title: En Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky assume d’ouvrir une crise politique avec son remaniement

Il a une nouvelle fois fait part sa volonté de réorganiser le système électoral aux Etats-Unis.

lemonde.title: Au-delà des dommages causés à la forêt, le feu de Fontainebleau suscite une « profonde tristesse »
lemonde.description: Naturalistes, randonneurs et autres amoureux du massif seine-et-marnais s’attristent de la disparition de riches écosystèmes et s’interrogent sur l’avenir d’un espace jusque-là très fréquenté, mais désormais fragilisé par le passage des flammes.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : les attaques américaines de la nuit en Iran ont fait huit morts et 20 blessés
lemonde.description: Téhéran a affirmé avoir frappé des radars américains à Oman ainsi que la base militaire d’Al-Tanf, en Syrie. Le Koweït, le Qatar et Bahreïn ont également été attaqués.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : entre une fidélité contrariée à leur parti et la tentation Edouard Philippe, les ministres LR cherchent leur place
lemonde.description: Suspendus depuis octobre 2025, les six membres Les Républicains du gouvernement Lecornu incarnent pour leur président, Bruno Retailleau, une page révolue : celle d’une droite alliée avec la Macronie. Les bannis estiment ne pas avoir trahi leur famille politique et plaident pour un candidat unique du « socle commun ».

lemonde.title: Les liens troubles avec la Russie d’un gestionnaire de mots de passe « européen »
lemonde.description: Passwork, qui se présente comme espagnol, a en réalité été développé en Russie et dispose toujours d’une licence du FSB, le service de renseignement intérieur russe. Ce qui soulève d’importantes questions de sécurité pour ses clients, parmi lesquels figurent des entreprises françaises.

lemonde.title: Xi Jinping appelle à une coopération mondiale sur l’IA, avec une approche « centrée sur l’humain »

lemonde.title: Protection de l’enfance : l’Assemblée nationale adopte le contrôle d’honorabilité pour tous les adultes en contact avec des mineurs, et la création d’une « liste noire »
lemonde.description: Les contrôles d’honorabilité, qui existent déjà pour les enseignants, ont été étendus à tous les adultes au contact d’enfants. Le texte prévoit également la création d’un fichier sur lequel figurera tout individu mis en cause pour des violences sexuelles sur mineur, même s’il n’a pas été condamné.

lemonde.title: Gel des retraites Agirc-Arrco : la CFE-CGC et la CGT saisissent la justice
lemonde.description: Face au refus du patronat de revenir sur l’absence de revalorisation des pensions complémentaires du privé, les deux syndicats, s’appuyant sur les 91 milliards d’euros de réserve du régime, tentent un recours devant le tribunal judiciaire de Paris.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : la FIFA annonce une enquête sur la banderole évoquant les Malouines brandie par des joueurs argentins

lemonde.title: Le Japon adopte une réforme de la succession impériale, l’idée d’une impératrice toujours exclue
lemonde.description: Le texte autorise le retour dans la famille impériale, par adoption, de parents masculins éloignés âgés de plus de 15 ans, à condition qu’ils soient célibataires. Il permet également aux femmes de conserver leur statut royal après avoir épousé un roturier, ce qui était déjà autorisé pour les hommes.

lemonde.title: Chez Saint-Louis, en Moselle : au royaume du cristal
lemonde.description: « Tour de France de savoir-faire d’exception » (1/5). Installée à Saint-Louis-lès-Bitche depuis 1586, la verrerie Saint-Louis doit sa renommée à ses pièces en cristal coloré aux motifs taillés en biseau, perle, étoile ou diamant. Un travail qui se décline sur des vases, des presse-papiers et des candélabres.

france24fr.title: France - Angleterre : une petite finale que personne n'a envie de jouer
france24fr.description: Boudé par les joueurs et souvent jugé sans intérêt, le match pour la troisième place de la Coupe du monde oppose, samedi, la France et l'Angleterre. spiegel.description: »Klatschfreundin« und »echte Matriarchin«: Der Kardashian-Klan hat sich mit Instagram-Beiträgen von Großmutter Mary Jo »MJ« Shannon, 91, verabschiedet. Nicht zuletzt habe sie ihr beigebracht, wie man eine Geschäftsfrau wird.

spiegel.title: Dieter Bohlen will Comeback von Modern Talkin mit Thomas Anders
spiegel.description: Dieter Bohlen würde gern erneut mit Thomas Anders als Modern Talking auftreten. Ein Veranstalter habe Konzerte angeboten, es gebe Vorschläge zu einer Doku und einem Musical. »Meine Hand ist ausgestreckt.«

spiegel.title: Extremwetter in Deutschland: Was uns die Hitze kostet
spiegel.description: Neue Daten beziffern die Folgen der jüngsten Extremtemperaturen für die Menschen und die Wirtschaft. Was jetzt passieren muss.

spiegel.title: AfD-Streit in NRW: Landeschef Martin Vincentz weist Alice Weidel scharf zurück
spiegel.description: Der AfD-Bundesvorstand verlangt den Abbruch der Listenaufstellung in NRW. Nun kontert Landeschef Martin Vincentz mit einem mehrseitigen Schreiben, das dem SPIEGEL vorliegt.

spiegel.title: AfD: Warum ein Vorgehen gegen Björn Höcke und seinen Landesverband schwierig ist
spiegel.description: Wenn ein Verbot der ganzen AfD so schwierig ist: Wie wär’s nur in Thüringen? Oder nur mit Björn Höcke? Das klingt einfacher, als es ist. Und lässt viele Probleme ungelöst.

spiegel.title: ZDF stellt »Ein Fall für zwei« nach 46 Jahren ein
spiegel.description: Raubein Matula war schon länger weg. Doch nun wird die Serie »Ein Fall für zwei« ganz eingestellt. Eine letzte Staffel 2027 und einen Spielfilm mit dem Anwalt-Detektiv-Duo will das ZDF noch zeigen, dann ist Schluss.

spiegel.title: Thomas Müller und Robert Lewandowski: Waldbrände verhindern Spiel in der MLS
spiegel.description: Bei den Bayern bildeten Thomas Müller und Robert Lewandowski einst ein Angriffsduo. Nun spielen sie in Nordamerika – aber vorerst nicht gegeneinander. Schlechte Luftqualität könnte auch das WM-Finale beeinträchtigen.

spiegel.title: Gesundheitsreform: Ministerin plant Verbot von Online-Krankschreibungen ohne Praxisbesuch
spiegel.description: Nicht in die Praxis und die Krankschreibung über Onlineanbieter bekommen? Angesichts der Debatte über eine frühere Krankschreibung wäre das ein Weg. Doch die Gesundheitsministerin will das unterbinden.

spiegel.title: Wetter: Todesopfer und Verletzte bei schweren Unwettern in Süddeutschland
spiegel.description: Umgestürzte Bäume, Überschwemmungen, herunterfallende Dachziegel: Schwere Unwetter haben Teile von Süddeutschland getroffen. Allein in Karlsruhe gab es mehr als 250 witterungsbedingte Einsätze. Ein Mensch starb.

spiegel.title: Danger Dan: »Dass der Intendant des ZDF anfängt, antifaschistische Lieder zu zensieren, ist leider ein furchtbares Zeichen«
spiegel.description: Harte Kritik, ein verweigerter TV-Auftritt: Mit seiner neuen Single sorgt der linke Liedermacher Danger Dan für Aufregung. Hier spricht er über die Auseinandersetzung mit dem ZDF, eigene Ängste – und seine Haltung zu Gewalt.

spiegel.title: Italien: Nicaragua bricht wegen Ex-Mitglied der Roten Brigaden Beziehungen ab
spiegel.description: Rom fordert die Auslieferung eines verurteilten Ex-Mitglieds der Roten Brigaden. Der Mann soll 1978 an der Ermordung von Premier Aldo Moro beteiligt gewesen sein. Nicaragua reagiert empört.

spiegel.title: Wie groß ist denn nun die Wohnung?
spiegel.description: Die Frage nach der Wohnfläche kann schnell zum Zankapfel werden. Welcher Anteil vom Balkon zählt zur Wohnfläche? Was gilt bei Dachschrägen? Und: Ist das Bad ein Zimmer? Hier kommen Antworten auf die drängenden Fragen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Fifa vergibt erstmals Ringe an Weltmeister
spiegel.description: Die Fifa lässt den US-Sport weiter mit dem Fußball verschmelzen und händigt dem Sieger von Spanien gegen Argentinien Ringe aus. Und: Die Falklandinseln fordern eine Strafe für Argentinien wegen eines politischen Banners. Alles Wichtige zu WM-Tag 37.

spiegel.title: Sexualstrafrecht: Umfrage zeigt breite Unterstützung für »Nur Ja heißt Ja«
spiegel.description: Eine neue Umfrage zeigt: 46 Prozent der Deutschen wünschen sich eine solche Änderung im Sexualstrafrecht. Besonders Jüngere sprechen sich dafür aus.

spiegel.title: Niedersachsen will Investor-Einstieg an VW-Standort Osnabrück absichern
spiegel.description: Volkswagen verhandelt mit dem israelischen Rüstungskonzern Rafael über eine Beteiligung am Werk in Osnabrück. Doch das Emirat Katar hat als Anteilseigner Vorbehalte. Jetzt will das Land Niedersachsen helfen.

spiegel.title: Brand im Müritz-Nationalpark: Alte Munition erschwert Löscharbeiten, Bundeswehr unterstützt
spiegel.description: Über 300 Hektar des Müritz-Nationalparks brennen, die Bundeswehr unterstützt bei den Löscharbeiten. Doch die erweisen sich wegen alter Munition im Boden als schwierig.

spiegel.title: Nato: Rutte sieht kein erhöhtes Eskalationsrisiko durch US-Raketen für Deutschland
spiegel.description: Mit Mittelstreckenwaffen aus den USA will Deutschland die Abschreckung gegen Russland verbessern. Nato-Chef Rutte spricht von einer »ausgezeichneten Nachricht« und hat auch eine Botschaft an Moskau.

spiegel.title: Ruf nach dem Gesetzgeber: DGB-Chefin Yasmin Fahimi fordert Hitze-Ausfallgeld
spiegel.description: Arbeitnehmer in Deutschland sehen sich im Hitzestress. DGB-Chefin Fahimi fordert Ausfallgeld für jene, die an solchen Tagen nicht mehr arbeiten können.

observador.title: Exames fantasma e o fechar de olhos de Montenegro
observador.description: Será que a sabedoria lusa nasce do cansaço de votar ou de ver o governo a ignorar o atraso dos exames, enquanto a oposição se afoga num tanque que queria ser piscina?

observador.title: As notícias das 9h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: O "catrapum" da Alemanha e os remates para Las Vegas
observador.description: Será que a poesia da bola se resume a um pé 43 biqueira larga, remates para Las Vegas e narradores a atravessar o Tejo a nado, ou é apenas o "vazio" da Alemanha a fazer "catrapum"?

observador.title: A Gulbenkian faz 70 anos. O que seria de Portugal sem ela
observador.description: A Fundação Gulbenkian ainda hoje é uma das 40 maiores fundações de todo o mundo, mas que papel ainda desempenha quando já não tem o petróleo e num país muito menos pobre do que o Portugal de 1956?

observador.title: Fica uma lição de vida para os alunos: não confiem em nada
observador.description: Os portugueses (que não querem eleições), Luís Montenegro (que ainda culpa o PS) e o ministro da Educação (que mantém o suspense) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.title: Guterres alerta para controlo de IA por países ou empresas
observador.description: Em conferência sobre IA, o secretário-geral da ONU alertou sobre a ameaça de "desigualdades ainda maiores". Destaca a necessidade de uma governação enraizada no direito internacional.

observador.title: Notas hoje mas só "à tarde", um atrelado na polémica com MAI
observador.description: Ministro pediu ajuda, mas professores recusam continuar avaliações. Atrelado apreendido pela PJ encontrado na Construbarcelos. O resumo do estado da Nação. E o novo episódio de "O Candidato Perfeito".

observador.title: No Coliseu do Porto, a criação artística não tem idade
observador.description: Depois de meses de actividades, as apresentações do Alquimia acontecem este fim de semana. O presidente da sala de espectáculos e a diretora do serviço educativo explicam motivos e objetivos.

observador.title: Polémica Senegal: médico da seleção é, afinal, ginecologista
observador.description: Enquanto o Senegal lida com a revelação de que o médico da seleção é ginecologista, a tensão entre Argentina e Inglaterra cresce com acusações de truques sujos e a polémica celebração de Enzo.

observador.title: 8h. MAI debaixo de críticas após divulgação de dois casos
observador.description: Montenegro disse no debate do Estado da Nação que mantinha a confiança política em Luis Neves. Ainda, sexta noite consecutiva de ataques dos Estados Unidos em territória iraniano.

observador.title: O "país caótico" que Luís Montenegro se recusa a ver
observador.description: O debate foi tenso, mas o primeiro-ministro lá se vai safando nas sondagens. Com as urgências a fechar e a oposição a morder-lhe os calcanhares, Montenegro joga à defesa para não perder o jogo.

observador.title: Brasil pode deixar de exportar carne para a Europa
observador.description: Setor teme perder acesso a mercado europeu por demora a adaptação a regras sanitárias da UE. Outros países podem impor limites à carne brasileira. País é o maior exportador mundial de proteína animal.

observador.title: Rui Ferreira e a Lux Records: 30 anos de rock em Coimbra
observador.description: A rádio mudou-lhe a vida, descobrir bandas e editar discos foi inevitável — só lhe faltar ser músico. Hoje tem uma loja de discos, organiza um festival e promete continuar a apostar em novos artistas.

observador.title: São Tomé e Príncipe termina campanha para as presidenciais
observador.description: As atenções viram-se para os comícios finais de Nito d'Abreu e Carlos Vila Nova, que tenta a reeleição. As eleições presidenciais estão marcadas para domingo; sábado é o dia de reflexão.

observador.title: Exames nacionais: "Processo cambaleante, novela mexicana"
observador.description: O presidente da Associação dos Diretores de Escolas Públicas espera que hoje as pautas sejam afixadas. Filinto Lima aponta para o horário a que as secretarias fecham, entre as 16h30 e as 17h30.

observador.title: Dezassete concelhos em risco máximo de incêndio
observador.description: Com temperaturas máximas entre os 23 (Porto e Viana do Castelo) e os 33 (Castelo Branco, Évora, Beja e Faro), mais de 60 concelhos estão em perigo muito elevado de incêndio.

observador.title: Trump acusa China de interferir nas eleições de 2020
observador.description: Num discurso à nação, Trump alegou que Pequim obteve ilegalmente registos de 220 milhões de eleitores, alegando que revelam "a maior violação de dados eleitorais da história".

observador.title: Porto. Decisão esta sexta sobre droga vinda do Brasil
observador.description: São 14 os arguidos acusados de vários crimes, nomeadamente tráfico de droga e associação criminosa. Principal suspeito importava droga desde 2020. Foi avaliada em cerca de 4,2 milhões de euros.

republika.description: L’età minima è 17 anni. Non è richiesta alcuna esperienza, serve una ottima conoscenza dell’inglese. La compagnia assumerà i candidati che avranno completato il programma e conseguito la licenza MPl (“nell’ambito del fabbisogno”)

republika.description: Il leader dei neocon all’epoca di Bush jr: “Sta facendo le prove generali per manipolare il risultato nel prossimo novembre”

republika.description: I sondaggi danno la maggioranza al centrista Yashar e all’opposizione il premier arriva a limitare gli aerei per non far votare la diaspora

nyt.title: Wildfire Smokes Makes Air Hazardous for Millions in Midwest and East Coast
nyt.description: The haze is likely to ease in the East this weekend but linger in the Upper Midwest, where some cities recorded extremely high pollution indexes on Thursday.

nyt.title: Canada’s Wildfires Are Burning Through the Night
nyt.description: As overnight temperatures climb across Canada, fires that once spread more slowly after dark are burning around the clock, straining fire crews.

nyt.title: What to Know About Canada Wildfire Smoke and Air Quality in U.S. Cities
nyt.description: A thick plume of smoke swept across the Midwest and New England, and those conditions could linger on Friday.

nyt.title: Ukraine Was on a Roll. Then a Clash Over War Strategy Exploded Into View.
nyt.description: From an underground parking garage, Ukraine’s newly dismissed defense minister aired the most dramatic, public critique of the military command to emerge during the war.

nyt.title: He Was a Russian Political Survivor, Until the Masked Men Appeared
nyt.description: Boris B. Nadezhdin, an outspoken opponent of the war in Ukraine, says he knows why he was detained: “Among our leadership, there is panic and chaos.”

nyt.title: Takeaways From Trump’s Speech Claiming Election Vulnerabilities and China Interference
nyt.description: Documents released by the Trump administration to support the president’s claims did not back up his most aggressive statements.

nyt.title: A Trump Obsession That Carries a Cost for Democracy
nyt.description: In demanding steps to address the integrity of voting, President Trump persisted in relitigating his 2020 election defeat while finding ways to cast doubt on the 2026 outcome.

nyt.title: In Prime Time, Trump Criticizes Networks for Not Carrying His Speech
nyt.description: The president also called for ABC and NBC to lose their broadcast licenses, after complaining that the networks were not airing his remarks.

nyt.title: Trump Released Documents on China and the 2020 Election. Here’s What We Know.
nyt.description: President Trump claimed that China had tried to acquire American voter data. Possessing such information would not allow votes to be manipulated.

nyt.title: Cyclospora Linked to Taylor Farms Lettuce Sent to Taco Bell
nyt.description: Federal officials worked with Michigan investigators to trace the outbreak to iceberg lettuce, which may also have gone to other vendors.

nyt.title: Astronomers Find an Atmosphere on a Nearby Earthlike Planet
nyt.description: It’s the first potentially habitable world known to host an atmosphere, making it a lead contender in the search for life beyond our solar system.

nyt.title: How Andy Burnham, ‘King of the North,’ Conquered U.K. Politics
nyt.description: A plain-spoken politician from a modest background in northwest England, Mr. Burnham is set to be named Labour leader — and prime minister apparent — on Friday.

nyt.title: New Prime Minister Faces Old Problems: How to Make Britain’s Economy Grow
nyt.description: Conversations with economists, and people around him, shed light on how Andy Burnham might tackle entrenched challenges.

nyt.title: How Andy Burnham Becomes Britain’s New Prime Minister
nyt.description: Andy Burnham is set to officially become the next prime minister on Monday, but a number of things have to happen before then. Here’s how everything is expected to play out.

nyt.title: Republican Rifts Deepen Over $95 Billion Budget Plan for Iran War and SAVE Act
nyt.description: A House panel approved the measure. But Republicans are divided over its size, cost and policy provisions, and many are concerned about the timing before the midterm elections.

nyt.title: Manhattan Building’s Buckled Columns Probably Lacked Required Reinforcements
nyt.description: Drawings obtained by The New York Times show the columns called for additional steel plates, but engineers reviewing site photos said they appeared to be missing.

nyt.title: Republican Senator Thom Tillis Demands Todd Blanche Meet With Epstein Survivors
nyt.description: Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina, a key vote on confirmation, had demanded the acting attorney general meet with victims.

nyt.title: White House Teleprompter Operator Bet on Trump Speeches, Kalshi Says
nyt.description: A technical assistant to President Trump won around $100,000, according to the prediction market, which flagged the activity to the federal government.

npr.title: China's Xi calls for step up of global effort in AI, as US curbs squeeze China's tech access
npr.description: American-led restrictions have blocked China from accessing some of the world's most advanced technologies, spurring China's efforts to build its own know-how and intensifying the tech race between the world's two biggest economies.

npr.title: Rubio convenes countries on left-wing political violence
npr.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday convened leaders from more than 60 countries to take part in the Trump administration's latest effort to quell what it calls "left wing" political terrorism.

npr.title: Japan revises law to ensure supply of (male) heirs to the imperial throne
npr.description: A popular princess drives support for having a female Japanese Emperor. But the country's first female prime minister opposes it.

npr.title: Boris Nadezhdin is a rare Russian politician speaking out against the Ukraine war
npr.description: Boris Nadezhdin wants to run for Russia's parliament on a platform that gives voice to the Russians against the war in Ukraine. That's why, he says, the Kremlin is doing everything to stop him.

npr.title: Hong Kong official warns booksellers on security risks after raids
npr.description: The police operation marks the third round of arrests targeting independent bookstores in four months.

npr.title: Zelenskyy fires Ukraine's tech-savvy defense minister in government reshuffle
npr.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has fired the country's popular defense minister, Mykhailo Fedorov, who pushed for innovation on the battlefield through use of drones and turned the tables on Russia.

npr.title: The political risks from war in Iran. And, ICE's use of force is rising, report finds
npr.description: The political implications the war in Iran is having on the GOP. And, a new report has found that ICE officers' use of force is not rare since President Trump took office for his second term.

npr.title: No Asian team managed to go far this World Cup (again). What's holding them back?
npr.description: For the sixth World Cup in a row, no team from the Asian Football Confederation made it past the first knockout round, winning only three games out of 29. Asian teams are competitive — up to a point.

npr.title: Dismissal of Ukraine's popular defense minister draws intense criticism
npr.description: As Ukraine signs drone deals and awaits licenses for Patriot missiles, the country's popular, tech-savvy defense minister, who helped Ukraine turn the tables on Russia through drone warfare, is fired.

npr.title: Venezuela's earthquake recovery overshadows its push for democracy
npr.description: After twin earthquakes killed thousands, Venezuela's recovery effort has pushed another crisis into the background: the fight for a return to democracy.

elpais.title: Trump resucita en un discurso a la nación el bulo del fraude electoral de 2020 y exagera la influencia de China en su derrota
elpais.description: El presidente desclasifica información en parte ya conocida y no vinculante, que incluye archivos de la CIA sobre Venezuela. El republicano está en una cruzada para arrojar dudas sobre las ‘midterms’, en las que los suyos llevan las de perder

elpais.title: Trump despide a su operador de teleprompter, acusado de apostar ilegalmente en Kalshi sobre sus discursos
elpais.description: El técnico, que trabajaba en la Casa Blanca, se embolsó casi 100.000 dólares por sus apuestas sobre las palabras que pronunciaba el presidente

elpais.description: Después del triunfo del seleccionado albiceleste ante Inglaterra en el Mundial de Fútbol, la Casa Rosada difundió una queja formal presentada con anterioridad

elpais.title: Morir en la quinta planta del Gregorio Marañón: “Aquí me dan paz y amor”
elpais.description: Javier del Río es paciente de paliativos en el hospital madrileño, centro de referencia para el final de la vida. En dos meses de estancia, además de la ayuda para que su dolor sea más llevadero, ha recibido visitas de amigos y ha organizado una fiesta

elpais.title: Volver a llenar el Mar de Aral: la apuesta de científicos españoles para evitar la liberación de millones de toneladas de CO₂
elpais.description: Los investigadores plantean en ‘Science’ financiar los trabajos de restauración del lago con créditos de carbono

elpais.description: El central de la Selección es el defensa que más pases buenos ha dado en la Copa del Mundo y el equipo ha mantenido la portería a cero en seis ocasiones

elpais.description: Como Diego en México 86, la Pulga necesitó que se construyera un entorno favorable para ejercer el liderazgo tanto en el vestuario como en el campo. El resultado: 15 goles en sus dos últimos Mundiales

elpais.description: ‘La Roja’ desactivó el saque de centro ensayado por el equipo de Deschamps con una propuesta de Alberto de la Fuente, el hijo del seleccionador

elpais.description: Entre los actores famosos que han encarnado al protagonista de la ‘Odisea’ antes que Matt Damon figuran Kirk Douglas, Armand Assante, Sean Bean y Ralph Fiennes

elpais.description: Con clásicos, ‘thrillers’, sorpresas muy literarias y novelas más ligeras, estas propuestas cubren todo el espectro de los aficionados al género. Pasen, lean y disfruten

phys-org.title: Bones reveal ancient Egyptian princesses born 4,000 years ago used weapons
phys-org.description: For decades, scientists have disputed the meaning of the weapons found in the burial chambers of some ancient Egyptian princesses. Were they symbolic or practical tools? Now, a reassessment of five royal women's mummies from the Middle Kingdom has shown that some princesses buried with weapons could use them.

phys-org.title: EU's AI 'guardrails' cannot absorb rapid changes in technology, study warns
phys-org.description: "Guardrails" built by the EU to govern AI fall short in both ambition and execution and have become too heavy to absorb rapid changes in technology, a new study in Big Data & Society warns.

phys-org.title: Golf generates nearly €630 million in societal benefits in Finland
phys-org.description: A new study published in Frontiers in Sports and Active Living shows that Finnish golf players spend approximately €330 million on golf annually and that this generates an estimated benefit to society almost twice as high.

phys-org.title: UN report offers roadmap for sustainable blue economies
phys-org.description: A new United Nations report co-authored by researchers at the University of Portsmouth provides governments with a practical roadmap for building sustainable blue economies, as pollution, climate change and biodiversity loss place growing pressure on the marine and freshwater ecosystems that support billions of people and a global ocean economy worth US$2.2 trillion.

phys-org.title: PathSay Project uses AI to cross language barriers

phys-org.title: For older women, water offers more than just physical health benefits

phys-org.title: Researchers discover rare freshwater mussels in Moosup River
phys-org.description: When University of Rhode Island researchers slipped beneath the surface of the Moosup River recently, they did not expect to find a living freshwater mussel community. The discovery marked the first documented record of freshwater mussels in the river in more than three decades and included rare native species considered sensitive indicators of river health.

phys-org.title: For biodiversity to thrive across Europe, laws should treat wildlife as individuals capable of suffering, experts argue
phys-org.description: Wildlife protection frameworks in both the EU and the UK need stronger and more consistent implementation—and must recognize animals as "individuals capable of experiencing suffering," rather than mere ecological assets.

phys-org.title: Algae fed by farm waste carpet Italy's warm River Po
phys-org.description: Rowers on the River Po in Turin are battling vast blooms of algae, as high temperatures in northwest Italy and runoff from farms create ideal conditions for rampant plant growth.

phys-org.title: Single fission experiment maps excess gamma rays from more than a dozen unstable nuclei
phys-org.description: In a single experiment, physicists have measured the "excess" emission of high-energy gamma rays from more than a dozen heavy, unstable atomic nuclei. Mapping the gamma-ray emissions of so many isotopes produced in nuclear fission marks an important step toward a better understanding of one of the key phenomena in modern nuclear physics: the fission process itself.

phys-org.title: Political representatives found more polarized on climate change than their constituents
phys-org.description: It is no surprise that there are political disagreements over climate protection measures. Parties differ in their assessments of which measures they consider effective, fair or economically acceptable. However, the question of whether climate change is mainly human-caused is not a matter of political preference but a well-documented scientific fact.

phys-org.title: Graphene nanoribbons survive gamma radiation, revealing potential sensors for fusion reactors
phys-org.description: University of Arizona researchers have demonstrated a promising new application for graphene nanoribbons, a nanoscale semiconductor material with the potential to withstand extreme environments. The team's findings could help clear a key hurdle to bringing fusion energy to the electric grid.

phys-org.title: Climate change reshapes waterborne disease risks as pathogens respond differently, review finds
phys-org.description: Climate change is altering the spread of waterborne diseases around the world, according to a comprehensive review published today in Nature Reviews Microbiology. The publication is the most up-to-date, comprehensive analysis examining how climate change influences waterborne diseases.

phys-org.title: The starry night redux: Dark energy camera captures stars, nebulae, clusters, and more in a rich, van Gogh-esque scene
phys-org.description: The 570-megapixel Department of Energy-fabricated Dark Energy Camera (DECam) captures a vibrant scene filled with swirls and stars reminiscent of Van Gogh's The Starry Night. This new cosmic masterpiece features the glowing nebula NGC 6729 on the left and the globular star cluster NGC 6723 on the right. DECam is mounted on the U.S. National Science Foundation Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile, a program of NSF NOIRLab.

phys-org.title: Can bacteria reveal hidden pollution? New river study says yes
phys-org.description: The Guadalquivir is the most important river in Andalusia. Stretching 657 kilometers (408 miles), it forms the backbone of Andalusia, from its source in the Sierra de Cazorla mountains to its mouth in Sanlúcar de Barrameda. These facts, along with its name of Arabic origin (Wadi al-Kabir) and its strategic role in the economy, agriculture and tourism, are widely known. Few studies, however, have comprehensively assessed the quality of the "Great River" along its entire course.

phys-org.title: How the trend for turning front gardens into driveways is adding to night‑time heat

phys-org.title: Glyphosate ban could cost Illinois farmers millions annually
phys-org.description: A new analysis from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the Illinois Soybean Association finds that Illinois corn and soybean farmers could lose up to $609 million per year—representing a 3.6% revenue loss—if the state banned the weedkiller glyphosate. The study is published in the journal Weed Technology.

phys-org.title: Living alligators expose why juvenile fossils can fool classification methods
phys-org.description: Fossil finds are exciting moments that sometimes introduce the world to an ancient mammal or dinosaur that existed millions of years ago. But a longstanding problem in paleontology is that fossils are often incomplete, and subtle differences between certain species, along with major changes that can occur as an animal grows, complicate species identification. undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

proj-syn.title: Where Will Global Financial Fragmentation Lead?
proj-syn.description: Debates about geopolitical fragmentation always revive the late economist Robert Mundell’s dream of a single world money. But participants should be mindful of the euro’s real-world experience over the past quarter-century.

proj-syn.title: Development Economics for an Age of Upheaval
proj-syn.description: The framework that has long guided development economics no longer reflects how modern economies actually create value. As the boundaries that once separated sectors become blurred, prosperity increasingly depends on how economies build the ecosystems that sustain technological progress and nurture new productive capacity.

proj-syn.title: The Death of the Degree
proj-syn.description: AI is often portrayed as a threat to higher education, with some administrators and professors focused on rooting out its use. But this approach fails to recognize that, in an AI-transformed world, the new dividing lines are technical capabilities and institutional pipelines that can quickly transform research into products.

proj-syn.title: Hungary’s Real Economic Test
proj-syn.description: Entering the euro with favorable market sentiment, but without an economy that can function well within a monetary union, would not serve Hungary’s long-term interests. It would be a formula for more broken promises—precisely the trend that the new government was elected to end.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Exposes the Global Economy’s Fault Lines
proj-syn.description: Buoyed by AI stocks, global financial markets have largely shrugged off the war with Iran. Yet the conflict’s long-term economic costs are only beginning to emerge, as depleted strategic oil reserves, damaged refining capacity, and rising fuel and fertilizer costs increasingly weigh on lower-income economies.

proj-syn.title: Governments Should Govern AI, Not Own It
proj-syn.description: AI systems are now powerful enough to threaten critical infrastructure, financial systems, and national security. Rather than becoming shareholders in AI companies, as US President Donald Trump has proposed, governments should invest in the independent institutions needed to hold the industry accountable.

proj-syn.title: The Tragedy of “Westalgia”
proj-syn.description: Some European leaders seem to think that abasing themselves for Donald Trump's pleasure is necessary to save NATO and keep the Western alliance alive. But by so desperately clinging to the good old days of the transatlantic relationship, Europe’s leaders are risking more than just their dignity.

proj-syn.title: The West’s Turkey Dilemma
proj-syn.description: Few countries better illustrate the difficult trade-off between democratic principles and strategic necessity than Turkey. As the country’s geopolitical and economic importance grows, NATO allies are becoming increasingly willing to overlook President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s attacks on democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: How the Tech Lords Hacked the Firm
proj-syn.description: A handful of tech oligarchs have figured out how to tap public markets without submitting to shareholder oversight. The recent SpaceX IPO represents the culmination of this process, granting Elon Musk near-total authority and revealing how thoroughly the mechanisms meant to hold corporate leaders accountable have been weakened.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Real Energy Test
proj-syn.description: The Iran war has underscored the fragility of global energy markets, exposing which economies can withstand repeated shocks and which cannot. For ASEAN+3 countries, resilience will depend on stronger electricity systems, regional cooperation, and institutions that can manage persistent uncertainty.

proj-syn.title: The US Economy Cannot Grow Without Renewables
proj-syn.description: Consumption demand, which has long powered America’s formidable economy, rests on the promise of cheap energy. But the Trump administration has conflated that with fossil fuels, confusing historic correlation with causation and, in the process, jeopardizing long-term prosperity.

proj-syn.title: The Purpose of Development Cooperation Is to Be Unnecessary
proj-syn.description: The original promise of development cooperation was to help countries overcome poverty, build productive economies, and reduce their dependence on external resources. That has not happened, and ongoing reviews of development cooperation, which focus on donor countries' needs and priorities, are unlikely to change this.

proj-syn.title: Oil Shocks Are No Longer So Shocking
proj-syn.description: Despite this year's US/Israeli-Iran war causing the largest-ever disruption to global oil supplies, the shocks of the 1970s had a greater impact. Because oil has been used as a weapon for so long, markets, policymakers, and strategists have adapted.

proj-syn.title: The Mother of All Economic Shocks Is Chinese Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Because analysts tend to put the United States at the center of the global economic story, they have overlooked the single most important force of the past 50 years. But it will be obvious to later generations that Chinese mercantilism has been more globally consequential than any other economic shock or policy choice.

proj-syn.title: Letting Russia Burn
proj-syn.description: From relentless Ukrainian drone strikes to soaring inflation and fuel shortages, Russia is paying an ever-higher price for Vladimir Putin's war of choice. But the war has become the organizing principle of Putin’s regime, leaving no path to lasting peace without a fundamental political transformation.

proj-syn.title: What AI Governance Demands
proj-syn.description: AI governance must account for everything from the technology’s material requirements to its effects on communities, businesses, labor markets, the environment, and strategic competition. To this end, a framework of verification-based trust—broader than national regulation and more flexible than a classic treaty—is essential.

proj-syn.title: A Japanese Wake-Up Call for America
proj-syn.description: Japan’s deepening currency and bond-market woes should be a wake-up call for other countries that appear to be on unsustainable fiscal paths, not least the United States, as well as France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. After all, a crisis in one country often draws investors' attention to others facing similar problems.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.
